newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends nearly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends nearly unchanged.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Thursday 0.15 percent higher with an excess of liquidity on the market, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 563.26 points from 562.42 points on Wednesday.
"There is too much money on the market, people are ready to buy anything, they are anticipating good annual results of blue chip stocks" a broker at Casablanca-based Wafa Bourse said.
Oil refinery, Samir, recently introduced on the gradual electronic trading, remained unchanged at 280 dirhams with 28,156 shares changing hands.
Steel mill Sonasid was up nine dirhams to 460 dirhams with 2,553 shares traded on the official market.
Only four companies are traded on the gradual introduction of electronic trading, and.
ONA group, the biggest private holding, edged up three dirhams to close at 718 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique fell nine dirhams after steady gains to trade at 190 dirhams with 18,616 shares exchanged.
Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing, which was listed on the bourse late in February, took eight dirhams to close at 303 dirhams with a volume of eight shares traded. Its initial price was 230 dirhams.
"The price does not reflect the real value of the company but since it's illiquid, it is expected to go even higher," he added.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, remained unchanged at 670 dirhams.
Brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc, shed one dirham to 1799 dirhams.
The company said on Thursday it posted a net profit of 162.5 million dirhams ($17.2 million) in 1996 from 139.2 million dirhams the year before.
Branoma, another brewery, added 30 dirhams to 1050 dirhams boosted by news of a net profit of 26.1 million dirhams ($2.7 million) last year from 21.6 million dirhams in 1995, up 20.8 percent.
Traded volume on the official market was 106.6 million from 130.6 million dirhams on Wednesday.
